summary: Illinois abolished the death penalty in 2011 when Democratic Governor Pat Quinn signed abolition legislation on March 9, 2011, effective July 1, 2011. Quinn also commuted the sentences of the fifteen inmates on Illinois' death row to life imprisonment. The note also notes criticism of Quinn, who had said during the 2010 gubernatorial campaign that he supported the death penalty, and who won that race with 50.4% of the vote against the Republican candidate.
one_line: Illinois abolished capital punishment in 2011 under Governor Pat Quinn, who also commuted the sentences of all fifteen death row inmates.
key_facts: Democratic Governor Pat Quinn signed legislation on March 9, 2011 to abolish the death penalty in Illinois.
The abolition legislation was set to go into effect on July 1, 2011.
Pat Quinn commuted the death sentences of the fifteen inmates on Illinois' death row to life imprisonment.
Pat Quinn was criticized for signing the abolition bill after saying he supported the death penalty during the 2010 gubernatorial campaign.
Pat Quinn defeated the Republican candidate in the 2010 gubernatorial election with 50.4% of the vote.
